910.name: Prehistoric Burma and Pyu City-States
910.description: Early human habitation in the Irrawaddy valley, the rise of the Pyu city-states as the first urbanized civilization in Myanmar, their sophisticated irrigation systems, and the devastating Nanzhao raids.

sub_clusters.name: Prehistoric Settlements
sub_clusters.description: The Anyathian stone tool culture, cave paintings at Padah-Lin caves, the Neolithic and Bronze Age communities of central Myanmar, and early rice cultivation in the Irrawaddy valley.

sub_clusters.name: Pyu City-States
sub_clusters.description: The Theravada Buddhist Pyu city-states of Sri Ksetra, Beikthano, and Halin, their sophisticated urban planning, water management, and the devastating Nanzhao raids from Yunnan that destroyed the Pyu civilization.
key_events: Sri Ksetra (near modern Pyay) becomes the largest Pyu city-state (c. 5th–9th century)
Nanzhao kingdom raids destroy the Pyu city-states (832–835 AD)

910.name: Mon Kingdoms
910.description: The Mon people's Dvaravati and Thaton kingdoms in Lower Burma, their role as the conduit of Theravada Buddhism, Indian culture, and literacy to the Burman people.

sub_clusters.name: Thaton and Lower Burma Mon Civilization
sub_clusters.description: The Mon kingdom of Thaton (Sudhammavati) in Lower Burma, its role as a major Theravada Buddhist center, trade connections with India and Sri Lanka, and its conquest by Anawrahta of Pagan.
key_events: Anawrahta of Pagan conquers Thaton and carries off Mon monks, scholars, and the Tripitaka (1057)

920.name: Pagan Empire
920.description: The first unified Burmese state under King Anawrahta, the extraordinary temple-building period that created over 10,000 monuments on the Bagan plain, and the empire's fall to the Mongols.

sub_clusters.name: Anawrahta and Burmese Unification
sub_clusters.description: The founding and early growth of Pagan, King Anawrahta's unification of the Irrawaddy valley, the conquest of Thaton, the adoption of Theravada Buddhism as state religion, and the beginning of massive temple construction.
key_events: Anawrahta unifies Burma and establishes Theravada Buddhism as the state religion (c. 1044–1077)

sub_clusters.name: Golden Age and Temple Building
sub_clusters.description: The reigns of Alaungsithu, Narathu, and Narapatisithu, the construction of Ananda Temple, Dhammayangyi, Htilominlo, and thousands of other monuments, and the golden age of Burmese Buddhist civilization.
key_events: Construction of Ananda Temple — masterpiece of Mon-Burman Buddhist architecture (c. 1105)
Over 10,000 Buddhist temples, monasteries, and pagodas built on the Bagan plain

sub_clusters.name: Decline and Mongol Invasion
sub_clusters.description: Excessive temple building draining state resources, the weakening of central authority, Kublai Khan's punitive expeditions, the Battle of Ngasaunggyan, and the collapse of the Pagan Empire.
key_events: Mongol forces invade and the Pagan Empire collapses (1287–1297)

930.name: Fragmentation and Shan States Period
930.description: The post-Pagan fragmentation into rival Shan, Mon, and Burman kingdoms — Ava, Pegu, Mrauk U — and the Forty Years' War between Ava and Pegu.

sub_clusters.name: Ava, Pegu, and Mrauk U
sub_clusters.description: The Shan-dominated kingdom of Ava in Upper Burma, the Mon kingdom of Pegu (Hanthawaddy) in Lower Burma, the Arakanese kingdom of Mrauk U, and their shifting alliances and wars.
key_events: Wareru founds the Mon kingdom of Hanthawaddy (Pegu) (1287)
Forty Years' War between Ava and Pegu devastates central Burma (1385–1424)

930.name: Toungoo Dynasty
930.description: The Second Burmese Empire under the Toungoo dynasty — Tabinshwehti and Bayinnaung's conquests creating the largest empire in Southeast Asian history, and its eventual decline.

sub_clusters.name: First Toungoo Empire
sub_clusters.description: Tabinshwehti's reunification of Burma, Bayinnaung's conquests of the Shan States, Lan Na, Laos, Ayutthaya, and Manipur — creating the largest empire in Southeast Asian history.
key_events: Bayinnaung conquers Ayutthaya and creates the largest empire in Southeast Asian history (1569)

sub_clusters.name: Restored Toungoo and Decline
sub_clusters.description: The collapse and restoration of the Toungoo dynasty at Ava, the more modest Restored Toungoo kingdom, engagement with European traders, and the Mon rebellion that ended the dynasty.
key_events: Mon forces capture Ava, ending the Toungoo dynasty (1752)

940.name: Konbaung Dynasty
940.description: The last Burmese dynasty — Alaungpaya's reunification, the destruction of Ayutthaya, the Anglo-Burmese Wars, and the British annexation of Burma in three stages.

sub_clusters.name: Alaungpaya and Konbaung Expansion
sub_clusters.description: Alaungpaya's rapid reunification of Burma, the destruction of the Mon kingdom, Hsinbyushin's sack of Ayutthaya, the repulsion of four Chinese invasions, and the founding of Rangoon.
key_events: Alaungpaya founds Rangoon (Yangon) and reunifies Burma (1755)
Burmese forces sack and destroy Ayutthaya, ending the Thai kingdom (1767)

sub_clusters.name: Anglo-Burmese Wars and Annexation
sub_clusters.description: The three Anglo-Burmese Wars progressively dismembering the Konbaung kingdom — loss of Arakan and Tenasserim (1826), Lower Burma (1852), and finally Upper Burma and the exile of King Thibaw (1885).
key_events: First Anglo-Burmese War — Burma cedes Arakan and Tenasserim to Britain (1824–1826)
Third Anglo-Burmese War — Britain annexes Upper Burma and exiles King Thibaw (1885)

940.name: British Burma
940.description: British colonial rule, Burma as a province of India, the rice export economy, the rise of Burmese nationalism, the Saya San rebellion, and the separation from India.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Administration and Economy
sub_clusters.description: Burma's annexation as a province of British India, the destruction of the traditional social order, the rice export boom, Indian immigration, and the foundations of colonial exploitation.

sub_clusters.name: Nationalist Movements
sub_clusters.description: The GCBA and Young Men's Buddhist Association, the Saya San peasant rebellion, the Dobama Asiayone movement, Aung San and the Thirty Comrades, and Burma's separation from India in 1937.
key_events: Saya San rebellion — a major peasant uprising against British rule (1930–1932)
Burma separated from British India and given its own constitution (1937)

950.name: World War II and Independence
950.description: The Japanese occupation, Aung San's BIA and the Anti-Fascist coalition, independence, the Panglong Agreement with ethnic minorities, Aung San's assassination, and the early democratic period.

sub_clusters.name: Japanese Occupation and Resistance
sub_clusters.description: The BIA's initial alliance with Japan, the Japanese occupation's brutal impact, the Burma Campaign (Kohima, Imphal), Aung San's switch to the Allied side, and liberation.
key_events: Battle of Imphal and Kohima — turning point of the Burma Campaign (1944)

sub_clusters.name: Independence and Early Democracy
sub_clusters.description: The Panglong Agreement promising ethnic autonomy, the assassination of Aung San, independence under U Nu, the KMT incursion, ethnic insurgencies, and the fragile parliamentary democracy.
key_events: Panglong Agreement — Aung San secures ethnic minorities' support for independence (12 February 1947)
Aung San and six cabinet members assassinated (19 July 1947)
Burma achieves independence from Britain (4 January 1948)

950.name: Military Rule and Socialist Period
950.description: General Ne Win's military coup, the 'Burmese Way to Socialism', economic isolation and decline, the destruction of democratic institutions, and the 8888 Uprising.

sub_clusters.name: Ne Win and the Burmese Way to Socialism
sub_clusters.description: Ne Win's coup, the nationalization of industry, the disastrous socialist economic policies, international isolation, the suppression of ethnic minorities, and the country's impoverishment.
key_events: General Ne Win seizes power in a military coup (2 March 1962)

sub_clusters.name: 8888 Uprising
sub_clusters.description: The nationwide pro-democracy uprising of August 1988, the emergence of Aung San Suu Kyi, the military's brutal crackdown killing thousands, and the formation of the SLORC junta.
key_events: 8888 Uprising — nationwide pro-democracy protests brutally suppressed by the military (8 August 1988)
Aung San Suu Kyi emerges as leader of the democratic opposition

960.name: SLORC/SPDC Junta Era
960.description: The military junta's refusal to honor the 1990 election results, Aung San Suu Kyi's house arrest, international sanctions, the Saffron Revolution, and Cyclone Nargis.

sub_clusters.name: 1990 Election Annulment and Repression
sub_clusters.description: The NLD's landslide victory in 1990 ignored by the military, Aung San Suu Kyi's Nobel Peace Prize and prolonged house arrest, the crackdown on ethnic minorities, and international isolation.
key_events: NLD wins 1990 election in a landslide; military refuses to hand over power
Aung San Suu Kyi awarded the Nobel Peace Prize while under house arrest (1991)

sub_clusters.name: Saffron Revolution and Cyclone Nargis
sub_clusters.description: The 2007 Saffron Revolution led by Buddhist monks, the military's violent suppression, Cyclone Nargis killing over 138,000 and the junta's obstruction of international aid, and the 2008 constitution.
key_events: Saffron Revolution — monks lead massive anti-government protests (September 2007)
Cyclone Nargis devastates the Irrawaddy Delta, killing over 138,000 (May 2008)

960.name: Democratic Transition and 2021 Coup
960.description: The partial democratic opening under Thein Sein, the NLD's 2015 election victory, the Rohingya genocide, the 2021 military coup, mass civil disobedience, and the ongoing civil war.

sub_clusters.name: Democratic Opening and Rohingya Crisis
sub_clusters.description: Thein Sein's reforms, the NLD's 2015 landslide, Suu Kyi as State Counsellor, the military's genocidal campaign against the Rohingya in Rakhine State, and international condemnation.
key_events: NLD wins landslide victory; Aung San Suu Kyi becomes State Counsellor (2016)
Myanmar military launches genocidal operations against Rohingya Muslims in Rakhine State (August 2017)

sub_clusters.name: 2021 Coup and Civil War
sub_clusters.description: The 1 February 2021 military coup, the Civil Disobedience Movement, the formation of the National Unity Government and People's Defence Forces, and the escalating nationwide civil war.
key_events: Military coup overthrows the elected NLD government; Suu Kyi arrested (1 February 2021)
Nationwide Civil Disobedience Movement and armed resistance against the junta

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
